HONEST ASSESSMENT OF DATA AVAILABILITY - THIS LITERATURE IS THIN, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE FINDING.
Systematic searching of PMC (NCBI E-utilities) and Europe PMC with ~20 distinct query formulations returned almost no papers whose PRIMARY purpose is measuring oligonucleotide toxicity in human iPSC-derived neural cells. Representative counts: PMC title/abstract query (antisense oligonucleotide[TI]) AND (iPSC OR induced pluripotent) AND (toxicity OR cytotoxic*) returned ZERO hits; (oligonucleotide) AND (neurotoxicity) AND (in vitro) AND (human) in title/abstract returned ONE hit, and it was unrelated (bilirubin in SH-SY5Y); (splice-switching OR morpholino OR PMO) AND (hiPSC OR iPSC) AND (neuron*) AND (viability OR toxicity) returned ZERO. Every usable row below was recovered by mining EFFICACY papers for their tolerability/control arms, not from dedicated toxicology studies. The file contains 121 measurements across 44 oligonucleotides and 20 distinct human (plus one rat comparator) model systems, drawn from 14 papers - but only ONE of those 14 (PMC12744863) was designed as an oligonucleotide neurotoxicity study, and even there the human arm is a neuroblastoma line rather than iPSC-derived neurons. Grade distribution is 71 grade-0, 23 grade-1, 18 grade-2, 9 grade-3, i.e. the lane is dominated by negative/tolerability rows, which is expected when the source material is control arms of efficacy papers. There is, as far as this search could establish, no published concentration-response cytotoxicity panel for a series of oligonucleotides in human iPSC-derived cortical or motor neurons. That gap is precisely what the NCATS challenge is asking to be filled, and it should be stated plainly in the methodology write-up rather than papered over.

Specific sub-modalities where I found NOTHING usable despite targeted searching:
- iPSC-derived MOTOR neurons with an oligonucleotide toxicity readout: none found.
- iPSC-derived ASTROCYTES or OLIGODENDROCYTES with an oligonucleotide toxicity readout: none found (the CEM paper quantifies uptake in GFAP+ astrocytes within a mixed culture but reads out transfection efficiency, not toxicity).
- NfL release into culture medium after oligonucleotide exposure in any human neural system: none found. The query (oligonucleotide) AND (neurofilament light OR NfL) AND (in vitro OR culture OR iPSC) in PMC title/abstract returned ZERO hits. In vitro NfL is a completely open niche.
- GFAP or IBA1/AIF1 induction measured in human iPSC astrocytes/microglia after oligonucleotide exposure: none found (AIF1/GFAP appear only as in vivo rodent histopathology criteria, e.g. in the n-Lorem screening cascade).
- Human brain microvascular endothelial / BBB models with a CNS-relevant oligonucleotide toxicity readout: none found.
- Human neuron-glia co-culture designed as a toxicity assay: none found; the closest is the mixed MAP2+/GFAP+ hiPSC culture in the CEM paper.
- Caspase-3/7 or TUNEL after oligonucleotide exposure in human iPSC neurons: only one TUNEL row exists in this file, and it is from an organoid EFFICACY experiment where apoptosis fell.

ASSAYS PROPOSED TO PREDICT CNS TOXICITY OF OLIGONUCLEOTIDES (found, but not row-able):
(a) n-Lorem's published CNS ASO screening cascade (PMC13227102, NAR 2026, 10.1093/nar/gkaf406-series; Table 1) specifies quantitative acceptance criteria: ~500 ASOs in a primary screen requiring >80% target reduction; five-point dose response in ~50-75 ASOs requiring IC50 <=1 umol by FREE UPTAKE; in vitro off-target analysis requiring ~10-fold separation between on-target and off-target IC50; a BJAB innate-immunity assay requiring <2-fold TNF-alpha increase at high ASO concentration; then single-dose rodent tolerability with AIF1/GFAP microglial and astrocytic histopathology; then a 3-month GLP study requiring therapeutic index >10. I did NOT convert these to measurement rows because they are acceptance thresholds, not measurements on named compounds, and forcing them into the per-measurement grain would corrupt it. They belong in the methodology narrative. Note the human cell lines in this cascade (BJAB) are lymphoblastoid, not neural.
(b) The stereodefined anti-tau PMO-gapmer programme (PMC11699249 and its commentary PMC12415975) used SH-SY5Y as an explicit cytotoxicity FILTER: ~20,000 designs narrowed in silico to 184 hit sequences, synthesised as stereorandom 5-8-5 2'-OMe PS gapmers, screened in SH-SY5Y with Lipofectamine RNAiMAX for 48 h, "65 active sequences [identified] after excluding the ones showing cytotoxicity". I did not create a row because the sources conflate exclusion-for-inactivity with exclusion-for-cytotoxicity, so the number of cytotoxic sequences is not separable from the 119 dropped. This is the largest human-neural-surrogate oligonucleotide cytotoxicity screen I located; its per-sequence data would be extremely valuable if the authors can be asked for it.
(c) The KCNT1 n-of-1 programme (PMC13099374) and the SCN2A n-of-1 programme (PMC13472884, Nat Med 2026, 10.1038/s41591-026-04527-y) both run a human-cell cascade: patient iPSC-neuron potency and allele selectivity, transcriptome-wide RNA-seq off-target analysis in human iPSC neurons benchmarked against tofersen and tominersen, plus a BJAB CCL22 innate-immunity assay at up to 8 uM. The SCN2A paper additionally validated three predicted off-target genes (ANKS1B, TXK, CFAP47) in a cell-based dose-response assay, finding dose-dependent reduction of ANKS1B and TXK; I did not create rows because the retrieved text does not name the cell line for that assay or give concentrations.
